The article names MOSFET, EVARM and Radi-N/Radi-N2 but does not describe them; their linked CSA pages were not ingested, so described_as is null rather than guessed. full_name is only set where the article's own link carries a title attribute (MOSFET).
The 30% neutron share is the CSA's rounded ('about') figure for the ISS, not a deep-space value.

extracts: The CSA has awarded a contract of $5.5 million to Bubble Technology Industries for the continued development of the CANS, a compact and autonomous instrument designed to measure neutron radiation exposure in space.
Neutron radiation, which contributes to about 30% of total radiation on the ISS, is especially harmful because it can cause serious biological damage and require specialized protective measures.
CANS improves upon previous radiation detection methods with the unique combined capabilities of working continuously and autonomously.
Canada has significant expertise in radiation detection experiments on the ISS, including MOSFET, EVARM and Radi-N and Radi-N2.
